units.function: Development watcher regression tests for filesystem disappearance races, missing signatures and deletion diffs.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> development snapshot script -> synchronous local filesystem or injected filesystem shim; no product server, deployment controller or domain layer.
units.keyDataModels: Watched directory/file lists, ignored paths, relative-path-to-signature snapshot map and changed/deleted path diff.
units.lifecycle: Scan watched paths -> tolerate disappearing entries -> compare metadata signatures -> trigger development restart for changed/deleted paths outside this suite.
units.testAssessment: Combined dev-runner Vitest passed 9/9; this file contributes 4 deterministic race tests. It omits content/hash fidelity, symlinks, permission errors, scale and actual restart behavior, but adequately guards the narrow development crash regression.
units.designRationale: Keep hot reload usable while editors/build tools atomically replace or delete files during directory traversal.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS development tooling needs reliable local iteration, but production deployment and execution-node reconciliation require stronger artifact and rollout guarantees.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Reuse the injected-filesystem race-test technique if Company OS builds a watcher; do not treat metadata snapshots as a production artifact/deployment contract. Production profiles need content-addressed signed artifacts, health checks, rollback and attestation.
units.responsibilityConflict: None in the narrow dev watcher, but it supplies no accountable change record or production artifact identity and therefore cannot participate in Company OS responsibility evidence.
units.securityFindings: LOW production relevance. Missing watcher cases include symlink escapes, permission errors, special files and unbounded trees. Metadata-only signatures may miss same-size/same-mtime content changes; this must not be reused for signed artifact identity or security decisions.

units.function: Development worktree tests for initialization markers, linked-checkout detection, environment precedence, migrated path repair and missing-env fail-fast behavior.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> dev-runner worktree bootstrap -> local repo/worktree files and caller-supplied process environment; no configuration schema validator, Secret store, Git command verification or deployment controller.
units.keyDataModels: Worktree root/.git file, seed-pending/complete markers, repo-local env path and PAPERCLIP_HOME/INSTANCE/CONFIG/CONTEXT/worktree variables.
units.lifecycle: Detect linked worktree -> block incomplete seed -> load repo-local environment without overriding explicit process values -> repair known stale paths -> report missing initialization.
units.testAssessment: Combined focused Vitest passed 9/9; this file contributes 5 tests. Positive precedence and fail-fast behavior are clear, but untrusted env parsing, filesystem provenance, concurrent setup and repair safety are not tested.
units.designRationale: Prevent development worktrees from accidentally sharing the main instance while allowing moved checkouts and explicit operator overrides to recover automatically.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs independent developer instances and safe self-hosted configuration migration without letting checked-out source silently redefine production identity/data paths.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY for explicit-env precedence and incomplete-initialization fail-fast patterns. Keep repo-local development configuration on an allowlist with path/owner checks; production managed/self-hosted profiles require versioned configuration commands, dry-run migration plans, backup/rollback and accountable evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: Repository-controlled environment files can alter instance and data/config paths without an accountable deployment action. Marker existence is not a signed or durable proof that initialization completed correctly.
units.securityFindings: HIGH configuration-injection concern: a repo-local env file can set instance/home/config/context paths; tests show no key allowlist, owner/mode/symlink/path-containment or secret policy. MEDIUM lifecycle gap: seed markers are trusted by existence, and stale paths are automatically rewritten in memory without dry-run, provenance or rollback evidence. Missing cases include malicious quoting/newlines, duplicate keys, traversal, concurrent bootstrap and moved/symlinked worktrees.
